broadcast.method: Which signal works where (v0.6): cell towers vs digital TV vs FM at our four sites.
notes: TV and FM: analytic link budget with the twin's calibrated loss and direct-signal cancellation; no co-channel neighbours (one transmitter per channel per area).
Cell towers: the twin's full design-point model (same sensors, same zone).
Located = 3 or more transmitter-sensor pairs detect the drone. FM resolves range only to ~1.5 km, so it can warn but not place a drone.
SIMPLIFICATIONS: licensed ERP toward the site; 8 dBi receive gain for TV, 2 dBi for FM; terrain beyond the site tile flat; 5 m error floor added.
CONSERVATIVE: against the published DVB-T trial (Martelli 2020, detection to 5 km bistatic) this model reaches only ~0.5 km; we keep it that way.
NOT MODELED: receiver blocking next to megawatt transmitters (Fulton is 6 km from a 869 kW station), ATSC 1.0 reference rebuild quality, terrain shadowing beyond the site tile.

calibration.source: Martelli et al. 2020, DVB-T AULOS trial (1.6-5 km bistatic)

gnss.method:
GPS jammer locator on the drone sensors (v0.6): detect a jammer and find it by time difference of arrival (TDOA).

Each perimeter sensor also listens on GPS L1 (1575.42 MHz). A jammer raises the noise floor at every sensor; the sensors
cross-correlate what they record and the differences in arrival time place the source (hyperbolic multilateration,
Gauss-Newton least squares; the method of the Baltic TDOA network, GPS Solutions 30:96, 2026).

Inputs and where they come from:
  * jammer: a car "privacy" jammer of 10 dBm (the DTU trial tracked one this weak, NAVIGATION 73(1), 2026) or a
    1 W (30 dBm) jammer, ~2 MHz wide around L1 (ASSUMPTION), 1.5 m above ground on a road;
  * propagation: the twin's terrain path model (free space + Bullington diffraction + ground reflection);
  * receiver: 3 dBi L1 patch, noise figure 2 dB with an LNA (ASSUMPTIONS), 10 ms correlation;
  * timing: the sensors' clocks are disciplined by GPS, which the jammer takes away. Each sensor then holds time on
    its own oscillator: an oven-controlled crystal (OCXO) drifts ~50 ns over a few minutes of jamming, a chip-scale
    atomic clock (CSAC) ~5 ns (ASSUMPTIONS, typical holdover figures). Clock error dominates; it is what we test.
  * TDOA noise per sensor pair: clock error (quadrature of both clocks) + correlation error 1 / (2 pi B_rms sqrt(2 SNR_eff))
    (STANDARD Cramer-Rao form), where SNR_eff = JNR x B x T.
Bearings: our sensors are 8-antenna rings, so each can also measure the direction the jamming comes from. The DTU trial
got 0.5-1 deg precision from a 5-channel array, with up to 10 deg bias before calibration; we use 2 deg (ASSUMPTION,
after calibration). Mode "tdoa+aoa" fits both together (weighted Gauss-Newton), which fixes the poor geometry when the
jammer sits outside a small ring of sensors.
Detection: a sensor detects the jammer when its jammer-to-noise ratio is above 10 dB (ASSUMPTION; GPS receivers lose
lock around 20-30 dB of J/N, so detection comes well before harm).

thermal.method:
Heat-camera cueing (v0.6): when our track points a thermal PTZ camera at a drone, how far out can staff see it?

Johnson criteria (STANDARD, used for thermal camera DRI ranges): pixels across the target's critical dimension needed
for a 50% chance of detection 1.5, recognition 6, identification 12. Pixels across = size / (range x IFOV), with
IFOV = pixel pitch / focal length. Camera (ASSUMPTION, typical uncooled security PTZ): 640 x 480 sensor, 12 um pitch,
35 mm lens (horizontal field of view ~12.5 deg) and, as an option, 100 mm. Atmosphere and contrast are ignored, so
these are upper bounds; a measured low-cost camera saw a Phantom 4 at only ~51 m (Univ. of Zagreb 2017).
Slew-to-cue: the camera turns at 60 deg/s (ASSUMPTION) and the drone must sit inside the field of view, i.e. the
track error must be smaller than half the view width at that range.

walkthrough.drone: Matrice 210 (5 kg, the Fraunhofer trial drone)

events.what: First track, 596 m from the drop point. Alert to the control room and the response team's phones.
Heat camera on the fence turns to the track (2.14 s at 60 deg/s); drone 746 m away.
Drone recognisable on the heat camera at 416 m (Johnson criteria, 35 mm lens).
Hovers 6 s over the drop point and releases the package.
Already moving to the drop point it was sent to at the first alert; recovers the package (South Carolina uses a pre-selected facility team; SCDC via Facilities Dive).

Track followed back out of the zone; its heading and the inbound track are kept as evidence and point the sheriff's K-9 team to where the pilot launched (the Georgia DOC pattern: staff alert the sheriff and K-9, who search and arrest).

cases.what: Drone reported about 5 a.m.; inmates picked up the package shortly after; the pilot walked out of the woods with a drone and a bag and was sentenced to a year and a day (WRDW, Nov 2026).
cases.lesson: Inmates reached the package before staff: the warning has to come before the drop, not after.

cases.what: Staff saw a drone carrying a duffel bag; the sheriff and K-9 were called and three civilians were caught that evening with 5 phones, 6.4 kg of tobacco and 1.2 kg of marijuana (Georgia DOC).
cases.lesson: The response playbook exists; it needs an earlier and more reliable trigger, and the launch direction.
